content.title: DESK JOB RULES FOR ANYONE SITTING 8+ HOURS A DAY
facts: **Stand every 30 minutes** – set a timer, even 60 seconds of standing wakes up your circulation and eases pressure on your spine.
**Move your screen up** – position it at eye level to stop the forward head tilt that strains your neck and shoulders all day.
**Roll your ankles** – do 10 circles each side hourly, it keeps blood from pooling in your lower legs while you're seated.
**Drink 1 glass of water** – every time you refill, you're forced to get up and walk, which breaks long stretches of stillness.
**Sit on your sit bones** – not your tailbone, this small shift protects your lower back from hours of slouched pressure.
**Stretch your hip flexors** – do a 20-second lunge stretch at lunch, sitting all day shortens them and can pull on your lower back.
**Take calls walking** – pace around during phone calls instead of sitting, it's an easy way to sneak in extra steps.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
If you sit for most of your workday, small habits matter more than one big workout after hours. Standing every 30 minutes isn't just about burning a few extra calories — brief movement resets blood flow to your legs and helps prevent the sluggish, heavy feeling that builds up after long stretches of sitting. Rolling your ankles hourly works the same way: it activates the calf muscles that act like a pump, pushing blood back up toward your heart instead of letting it settle in your lower legs. And that hip flexor stretch at lunch matters more than people think — sitting keeps those muscles in a shortened position for hours, and over time that tightness quietly pulls on your lower back and changes how you stand. Everyone's body holds tension differently, so notice where yours tends to stiffen first.
